flows.period: week ending Wed 11 Nov 2026 (BofA/EPFR + separately Reuters/LSEG Lipper; this is PRE-selloff data -- the next editions, due ~19-20 Nov, will be the first to cover the week including the Mon-Tue 16-17 Nov risk-off)
flows.narrative: Two independent trackers of the same week (ended 11 Nov) give directionally similar but not identical totals, reported separately rather than conflated: BofA/EPFR logged global equity inflows of +$98.3bn (largest since June 2026, led by a 6th-straight-week +$63.6bn US inflow and a 5th-straight-week China inflow, cumulative 5-week China total a record +$88bn) alongside a -$17.9bn money-market outflow. Reuters/LSEG Lipper's larger 29,202-fund universe instead shows Europe as the week's biggest single draw (+$35.13bn, strongest since June 2021, ~69% of its measured global total) on strong earnings and lower oil, with US equities +$6.6bn and EM equities +$4.65bn (3-week high) by its methodology, plus a sharp -$37.48bn money-market reversal (vs +$174.22bn the prior week). Both trackers agree gold ETF flows stayed modestly positive (+$49m BofA / +$614m Lipper) even as the gold price fell toward 14-month lows -- a price/flow decoupling flagged explicitly by EPFR commentary. Separately, China's domestic 'national team' bought a net 590.77bn yuan (~$82.9bn) of equity ETFs from October through 9 Nov across 23 consecutive trading days, consistent with the EPFR-measured China inflow streak. None of this yet reflects the Mon-Tue 16-17 Nov selloff; the next weekly cuts (due ~19-20 Nov) are the ones to watch for the first read on whether this was a genuine flow reversal or a sentiment-only move.
